answer: One workable design: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because harbor only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, vertex is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any orchard approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
